findings.title: The active Arduino verifier cannot pass fresh-run compilation
findings.criterion_ref: Criterion 10: “A real fresh graph-v9 N00→N90 cascade through N70/N80 is honest and executable.”
findings.trigger: Run real D01→D02 with the active Arduino v5 curriculum and target L01.
findings.consequence: D02 fails before effective-run compilation, so a fresh cascade cannot execute the live N70/N80 product path.
findings.evidence: The real probe returned D01 `inputs_frozen` with 78 inputs, then D02 `schema_contract` failure: `domain verifier source uses dynamic code or process execution`. `runtime/langgraph_factory/nodes/inputs.py:805-816` treats every attribute call named `compile` as forbidden, while `curricula/arduino_kit/verify_domain.py:59` legitimately calls `re.compile(...)`. The RC19 boundary probe independently produced the same baseline failure.

findings.title: D02 does not inspect executable verifier dependencies
findings.criterion_ref: Criterion 2 requires D02 to bind the complete verifier closure and reject “dynamic-code, native, and process-launch verifier surfaces before entry.”
findings.trigger: Declare `helper.py` as a verifier dependency, import it from the entry point, and put both `import subprocess` and `eval(...)` in that dependency.
findings.consequence: Process-escape and dynamic-code surfaces cross the pre-entry boundary and execute during D08 despite D02 reporting successful compilation.
findings.evidence: `qa_rc21_adversarial_probe.py:197-218` reproduced `d02_result: effective_run_compiled`, `d08_result: PASS`, and candidate output `dependency-dynamic-code-loaded`. `inputs.py:777-817` parses only the entry point; dependencies are merely frozen at lines 818-837.

findings.title: os.chdir exposes an undeclared engine-path existence oracle
findings.criterion_ref: Criterion 4 requires existing-versus-absent path oracles to be normalized or blocked; criterion 6 requires undeclared repository rename changes not to alter the same candidate/frozen-contract verdict.
findings.trigger: A D02-valid verifier constructs an undeclared engine-directory path, calls `os.chdir`, and the directory is then renamed without changing the candidate or contract.
findings.consequence: The identical candidate and frozen contract change from PASS to FAIL solely because an undeclared repository path was renamed.
findings.evidence: The executed probe reported identical candidate and contract SHA-256 values; with the directory present it returned PASS/0 and `undeclared-existing: visible`, while after rename it returned FAIL/1 and `undeclared-absent: visible`. `transport.py:754-825` guards open/stat/list/readlink/access but not `os.chdir`.

observations: All graph/spec/schema/contract hashes recomputed as claimed, including immutable graph-v8 `c2d79a…` and distinct graph-v9 `5236bf…` lineage.
Real plan validation, complete-tree scan, and ownership verification passed with 75/75 claims. Plan 26 status reported N13 PASSED and no stale receipts.
The package suite passed 176 tests; the full runtime suite passed 1355 tests, skipped 2, and passed 419 subtests.
RC19 candidate-overwrite repair, external engine-nested staging, read-only sandboxing, pre/post hashing, staged conflicts, and declared-drift regressions passed their existing tests.
reasoning: Execution confirmed three criterion-defeating failures outside the passing regression suite. I did not promote passing hash, staging, immutability, lineage, ownership, or suite checks to findings. The fresh-entry failure is deterministic and occurs before model work; the other two probes demonstrate an incomplete D02 code boundary and a verdict-changing undeclared-path oracle.
